AI vs AI · After-action report

Genghis's ArmyversusFlamebringer's Immortals

The Golden Khaganate under Genghis Khan against Ardashir the Flamebringer and his Javidan Immortals, on the Acropolis. The closest of six: the Khaganate led after three rounds, then Ardashir and the Immortals destroyed both Stormrider squads and a burning field on the centre did the rest, 34 to 25 in Round 6. Over the six battles the Immortals won 5 to 1, on average 33.2 VP to 21.7, and dealt more than three times the damage.

Flamebringer's Immortals win on Victory Points, 34 to 25 25 : 34 VP

Deployment

The Khaganate set up along rows 12 and 13: Genghis Khan leading the Khesig Guards at (5,12), the Black Shaman with Stormrider 1 at (3,13), Stormrider 2 at (11,13), the Nerge Outriders at (9,13) and the Tamga-Bound Troops at (6,12). The Atashid Empire set up on row 2: Ardashir leading the Javidan Immortals at (9,2), the Mobad with Shieldbearers 1 at (11,2), Shieldbearers 2 at (5,2), the Adur Furnace Guard at (3,2), and the two Sagdid Hound-Keeper squads at (7,2) and (10,2).

Commentary

  1. Command

    Neither side spends CP. Missions: FOCUSED FIRE for the Khaganate, DEEP REACH for the Empire. Primaries: BLEED THEM WHITE for Genghis, ERADICATE THE FOE for Ardashir.

  2. Movement

    Every unit Advances. Stormrider 1 and the Black Shaman reach the centre at (6,8), Genghis and the Khesig Guards the west at (2,8), Stormrider 2 the east side at (11,9). The Immortals come up to (9,5), the Shieldbearers to (8,5) and (10,4).

  3. Cleanup

    The Khaganate holds the centre and the west. Genghis's Army 5, Flamebringer's Immortals 0.

Battle Round 2

Ardashir drives off the riders

VP
10:7
Units standing
8:9
HP on the field
120:81

Commentary

  1. Command

    Genghis's Scouting Order on the Nerge Outriders spots the Mobad and Shieldbearers 1; he requisitions a Tamga-Bound squad. Ardashir spends 3 CP on Judgement of the Sun, which BLINDS Genghis and his Khesig Guards, and requisitions a Shieldbearer squad.

  2. Movement

    Ardashir and the Immortals charge Stormrider 2 on the east at (12,8); the riders Fall Back in disorder (3 HP). COORDINATED PUSH completes for the Empire (+2).

  3. Action

    The Tamga-Bound Troops shoot the Shieldbearers for 3. The Black Shaman's Chant of the Kindling raises Genghis's hunger.

  4. Cleanup

    The Khaganate holds the centre and the west, the Empire the east, with DEEP REACH (+3). Genghis's Army 10, Flamebringer's Immortals 7.

The damage record

Every unit that dealt damage, best first. Damage counts melee, shooting, spells and abilities; a joined pair's damage is split between the two units that took it.

The scoring record

Who scored the VP. At every scoring moment the engine was asked what would have scored with some of the side's units absent: a unit's share is its extra VP averaged over every order its side's units could have arrived in (its Shapley value), so the shares add up to the VP scored. "Hinged on it" is the objective VP its side would have lost had that one unit not been there, the rest of the battle as it was. VP no unit decided (an objective held by capture, a no-losses card): Flamebringer's Immortals 4 VP.

The activity record

What each unit did with its 1 APt a Battle Round. A move in the Movement Phase costs Movement Points, not APt, so a unit that only walks scores as idle: that is the wasted round this record is for.

Moves undone

A move the unit's next move undoes is a turn spent getting nowhere, as in chess when a piece goes and comes back while the other side develops. A pair counts when the second move takes the unit back beside where the first began, or away again from an objective the first moved toward, no nearer than it started. A CHARGE or a Fall Back is a fight's move and does not count. In this battle 3 of 63 moves were undone.

Passive rules

Rules that act without being used: an aura, a combat effect, an army's identity. Each attack one touched is priced by the rules' own estimate with the rule on its owner and with it off; at each Movement Phase's start, the units a rule held still, slowed or kept from squares are counted, each asked of the rules with the rule taken off.

The support record

Analysis

The Immortals win, and win the trade

Flamebringer's Immortals won 5 of the 6 battles, on average 33.2 VP to 21.7. They won every source: objectives 20.5 to 14.0 a battle, the Primary 5.3 to 2.3, the secondaries 7.3 to 5.3. The trade was lopsided: the Empire dealt 106.3 damage a battle and lost 35.3 RP; the Khaganate dealt 30.8 and lost 114.3, more than half its army. Genghis's one win was on Twin Lakes, 39 to 27.

Genghis's Army vs Flamebringer's Immortals: 6 battles on ACROPOLIS, CROSSROADS, TRIPLE HILLS, TWIN LAKES, seeds 1120, 1121, 1122, 1123, 1124, 1125.

Who scored

The Javidan Immortals (30 RP) scored 5.4 VP a battle, 18.0 per 100 RP, and were never destroyed; Ardashir (75 RP) 3.7, never destroyed, and in the featured battle he destroyed two Stormrider squads. The Shieldbearers (17 RP, 22 squads with requisitions) scored 3.3 a squad, 19.5 per 100 RP. For the Khaganate, Genghis (70 RP) scored 4.4 a battle; the Stormriders (20 RP) 2.3, destroyed 8 times in 12; the Tamga-Bound Troops (10 RP) 1.1, destroyed 12 times in 18.

What the AI did with them

  • Alchemical Vial, twice a round. The Shieldbearers used their Vial (+1 MS, BS and DEF this round, 2 charges) 32 times, and 16 of those were a second Vial on the same unit in the same round. A second Vial only refreshes the first, so it changed nothing and threw a charge away. Fixed after this batch: the AI now prices a buff the unit already holds from the same source at nothing.
  • Standing in the fire. Sunburst's BURNING FIELD covered the centre objective from Round 4 of the featured battle, and the Khaganate kept charging back into it to hold the centre; the burning destroyed the Khesig Guards and two Tamga-Bound squads.
  • Commands that bought nothing: Judgement of the Sun (3 of 3), Genghis's Double Time (7 of 7), Chant of the Kindling 11 of 18.
  • The Adur Furnace Guard were idle 4.0 Battle Rounds a battle and the Immortals 3.2, mostly standing on objectives they were holding.

How sure

Five to one, with the losing side losing more than half its RP each battle, is a clear result: the Immortals and Ardashir out-fought everything the Khaganate sent at them, and the Khaganate's cheap units died faster than they scored.

What to look at next

The Khaganate's light cavalry and Tamga-Bound charged into the Immortals and died. That is the losing-fight charge from today's findings: worth replaying once the charge pricing changes. And a burning field over an objective is worth a look at how the AI weighs the hazard against holding the ground.
